source_text: Post aliquanta iterum dicit Scriptura divina: cognovit Adam Evam uxorem suam, et concepit et peperit filium, et vocavit nomen eius Seth dicens: Suscitavit mihi Dominus semen aliud pro Abel, quem occidit Cain Ad documentum instituti coitus ipsum semen divinitas dicitur excitasse
pass_a_gloss: After some things divine Scripture says again: Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Seth saying: The Lord has raised up for me other seed in place of Abel, whom Cain killed. For a proof of instituted intercourse the deity is said to have raised up the seed itself.
pass_b_english: A little later divine Scripture says again: “Adam knew his wife Eve, and she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Seth, saying: The Lord has raised up other seed for me in place of Abel, whom Cain killed” (Genesis 4:25).
To demonstrate that intercourse was instituted [by God], the deity is said to have raised up the seed itself.

choices.why: Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
